cuerpo: 000 ABNT20 KNHC 211154 TWOAT Tropical Weather Outlook NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL 700 AM EST Sat Nov 21 2026 For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America: Offshore of the Southeast U.S. Coast: A large non-tropical low pressure area centered a few hundred miles east of northeastern Florida continues to produce disorganized showers and thunderstorms. The system is moving into an environment that will probably not be conducive for development of significant tropical or subtropical characteristics. Although the chances of tropical development continue to decrease, this large weather system is still expected to produce gusty winds, dangerous surf, rip currents, and coastal flooding along portions of the southeast and mid-Atlantic U.S. coasts into early next week. In addition, heavy rainfall and the threat of flash flooding will move northward over coastal portions of the Carolinas and the mid-Atlantic through the weekend. Interests along the U.S. East Coast should continue to monitor the progress of this system.
